g10-history-uh8-t1.overview: The 1991 Transitional Charter and the Formation of TGE sits inside Post-1991 Developments in Ethiopia. Transitional government and federal reform followed 1991 in Ethiopia, the focus of Unit 8 of Grade 10 History in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it explains the 1991 Transitional Charter and the Transitional Government of Ethiopia. Then it sets out the 1995 constitution and the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. Next, it traces the hydro-politics of the Nile (Abay) basin. Also it covers the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam and the Nile agreements. Finally, it looks at development and the challenges of democratization. Students will also learn how federalism applies to real-life situations, such as shared rivers and regional rights today.
objectives: Describe the 1991 Transitional Charter and the Transitional Government.
Explain the main features of the 1995 FDRE constitution.
Distinguish the nine regional states of the Ethiopian federation.
Trace the hydro-politics of the Nile and the major agreements.
Assess the aims of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam.
g10-history-uh8-t1.simple:
The 1991 Transitional Charter and the Formation of TGE in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the EPRDF, the fall of the Derg, and the London Conference of 1991.
  • The Transitional Government of Ethiopia and its 87-member Council of Representatives.
  • Also the 14 self-governing regions and the road toward a federal system.
g10-history-uh8-t1.detailed:

  • Explain the main features of the 1995 FDRE constitution.
  • Distinguish the nine regional states of the Ethiopian federation.
  • Trace the hydro-politics of the Nile and the major agreements.
  • Assess the aims of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam.
